title: Patch: an attack whose only kill is Cleave's splash counts as a killing trade

# #1821: Patch: an attack whose only kill is Cleave's splash counts as a killing trade
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The practice AI always weighs an attack that kills its target at an even trade before it spends mana — but only when the target itself dies. A Cleave attacker's best attack is often the one whose splash kills the neighbours while the target survives; today that attack is filed with the weak attacks and may never be simulated. After this change an attack counts as a killing trade when the target or any splashed neighbour dies.

## Why

`even_trade` (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:316-319`) gates on `trade.kills`, defined at `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:71` as "whether the strike kills the target itself". Splash kills only feed `cleave_value` (`reply.rs:104-105`). So a Cleave 4/4 hitting a 5/5 flanked by two 2/2s — the attack's entire payoff — has `kills == false`, lands in `other_attacks` after `round_robin(plays)` and `answers` (`candidates.rs:835-837`), and the beam's `root_branching` truncation (`crates/ai/src/search.rs:182-186`) can cut it before it is ever simulated. Same shape as the accepted #1779, which put each attacker's best even trade beside its free kills.

## Proposal

Add a `kills_any` flag to `Trade`, set when the target or any splashed neighbour dies — the `splash.kills` loop at `reply.rs:104` already computes it — and gate `even_trade` on it instead of `kills`. Do not relax the gate to `value > 0`: that would promote every chip attack (`chip_per_damage` is positive for any hit).

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/`. Engine and spec untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Cleave attack whose only kills are splashed neighbours passes `even_trade`.
- [ ] An ordering test puts such an attack ahead of the plays, the #1779 spot.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` smoke reports no regression.

## Size and risks

Small — plausibly easy: ~15 lines plus a test in one crate, one flag beside a field that already flows through. Low risk: a strict superset of today's promotion, never a new attack.
